why: The Fenwick tree's home ground: scan left to right, keep a count per value rank, and each answer is a prefix sum (how many earlier values have a smaller rank) followed by a point update.
hints: For each position you need 'how many of the values seen so far are smaller'. Which structure answers prefix counts while you keep inserting?
Rank the values (sorted distinct values -> 1..m). Before inserting nums[i], the answer is the prefix sum of counts over ranks 1..rank-1.
Fenwick tree: query by i -= i & -i, update by i += i & -i. Query, append, then add 1 at the rank. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Equal earlier values do not count: query rank - 1, not rank.
Values reach 10^9 and can be negative; compress them to ranks first.
A sorted list with insort is O(n^2) in the worst case.
